mutants.old:
ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT intents_idempotency_key_key DO NOTHING
RETURNING id
mutants.why: The intent insert no longer ignores a repeated idempotency key, so the same event delivered twice is not absorbed into one intent.
Self-skip compares the actor account with the store id instead of the recipient account id.

mutants.old:
ON CONFLICT (account_id, audience, store_id, aggregation_key) WHERE aggregation_key IS NOT NULL AND read_at IS NULL
DO UPDATE SET
    params = CASE WHEN EXCLUDED.occurred_at >= notification.inbox_items.occurred_at THEN EXCLUDED.params ELSE notification.inbox_items.params END,
    occurred_at = GREATEST(notification.inbox_items.occurred_at, EXCLUDED.occurred_at),
    actor_account_ids = ARRAY(SELECT DISTINCT a FROM unnest(notification.inbox_items.actor_account_ids || EXCLUDED.actor_account_ids) AS a ORDER BY a),
    updated_at = GREATEST(notification.inbox_items.updated_at, EXCLUDED.updated_at)
RETURNING id
mutants.why: The inbox write becomes a plain insert, so a second unread notification with the same aggregation key no longer merges into the existing row.
The worker no longer stops when the recipient account is already deleted, so an intent arriving after deletion still writes inbox and delivery rows.
The stored aggregation key drops the type prefix, so two types with the same raw key can merge into one inbox row.

mutants.old: params = CASE WHEN EXCLUDED.occurred_at >= notification.inbox_items.occurred_at THEN EXCLUDED.params ELSE notification.inbox_items.params END,
mutants.why: A merge overwrites params in job-processing order, so an older event processed last replaces the newer event's params.
The retry check no longer consults the intent link table, so re-running a merged intent after its row was read creates a duplicate row.
A delivery record is written without its channel job, so A8-3 would have nothing to run.
